head: b9696bd
target: Session start unsets a repo's hooks path when it names a missing directory, and the gate never writes into a hooks directory that another tool owns.
incidental: selftest scenarios for the stale hooks path and the manager-owned hooks directory

questions.prompt: A repo stops tracking its hooks directory, and a clone pulls that deletion. The clone's hooks path still names the deleted directory. Why does a push from that clone run with no gate?

options.label: Git falls back to the default hooks directory, which has no gate hook in this clone.
Git looks for hooks only in the directory the hooks path names, and that directory is gone.
The pull removed the repo's opt-in marker, so the clone is not gated anymore.

key_points: Git runs hooks from the directory the hooks path names, and from nowhere else.
The named directory no longer exists, so git finds no pre-push hook and runs none.
The failure is silent: nothing errors, and the push goes through.

questions.prompt: In another clone, the hooks path names a real directory that a hook manager owns. What could go wrong if the gate put its hook there, and what does it do instead?
key_points: Two tools would then fight over one hook file in that directory.
The manager may rewrite the file, so the gate could vanish without anyone noticing.
The gate writes nothing there and prints the line a human can add to the manager's pre-push hook.
Until a human adds that line, the clone's pushes run ungated, and the gate accepts that cost.

questions.prompt: A clone's local hooks path names a deleted directory. The author runs the installer by hand, before session start has run. Which of these happen?

options.label: The installer unsets the hooks path.
The clone is gated again once session start has run.
The installer writes its hook into the default hooks directory.
The installer prints the line a human can add to a pre-push hook.

key_points: Only session start unsets a stale hooks path; the installer never changes the config.
Any hooks path set in the config makes the installer refuse and print the line to add.
Session start then unsets the stale value and installs the gate's hook in the default hooks directory.
So the pushes are gated after session start, not after the hand-run install.
